XLF closed at a 52-week high as short rates fell faster than long ones, and JPM clears Cecil's $355 trigger, sits 0.5% under its high and has the book's lowest volatility (1.7% weekly).

The largest SPY weight and the AI leader sits about 5% under its 52-week high and tends to rise into earnings (Aug 26), but the size stays modest because SMH is still below its $595 50-day average and semis react most to CPI.

thesis: SPY rose 3.5% to within 0.5% of its all-time high after the -23K NFP cut September hike odds from about 55% to 44%. With VIX at 14.9, the 10Y at 4.66% and no major earnings, the week turns on Wednesday's CPI (core consensus +0.2%, with rebound risk after June's 0.0% and the Apple price hikes), then PPI, claims and retail sales. Against an SPY benchmark, cash is a direct bet against the market, so I hold 15% as a CPI buffer instead of the Council's 30% and keep the book's beta near 0.9. All five names come from the Council's own wikis and watchlist, sit near 52-week highs with fresh earnings momentum, have no scheduled binary event this week, and react to CPI in different ways: AMGN (defensive healthcare) and JPM (low-volatility financials at a breakout) anchor the book, while NVDA, ETN and AMZN give AI-leadership exposure so a cool print doesn't leave the book behind the way SYM and REGN did last week. I skip the CSCO and AMAT earnings, REGN's FDA decision and last week's biggest spikes (NEM +21%, QCOM +14%, INTC +13%).
risks: A hot core CPI (0.3% or more) would revive hike odds and hit NVDA, ETN and AMZN hardest, while a cool print could send high-beta semis up faster than the 15% cash, AMGN and JPM can keep pace; the wikis also contradict each other in places (dates, prices), which adds model risk. My training data ends months before this week, I have no memory of how it went, and I used none.
